# core/print.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/print.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Writing text and numbers to the serial console. Works
on every target: the console is standard output on the hosted target and
COM1 under a kernel.

`import "core/print.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/num.bastio](core-num.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`print_str`](#print_str) | The bytes of a literal. |
| [`print_span`](#print_span) | Bytes `from..to` of `b`. |
| [`print_bytes`](#print_bytes) | All of `b`. |
| [`print_text`](#print_text) | A text built with core/text.bastio. |
| [`print_nl`](#print_nl) | A newline. |
| [`print_u64`](#print_u64) | `x` in decimal. |
| [`print_u64_pad`](#print_u64_pad) | `x` in decimal, padded on the left with spaces to `width` bytes. |
| [`print_i64`](#print_i64) | `x` in decimal, with a `-` when negative. |
| [`print_hex`](#print_hex) | `x` in hexadecimal with a `0x` prefix. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `print_str`

```bastio
fn print_str(con: &Serial, s: Str)
```

The bytes of a literal.

Example:

```bastio
print_str(con, "pid ");
print_u64(con, 42);
print_str(con, ", offset ");
print_i64(con, -16);
print_str(con, ", flags ");
print_hex(con, 255);   // 0xff
print_nl(con);
print_u64_pad(con, 7, 4);
print_nl(con);
```

### `print_span`

```bastio
fn print_span(con: &Serial, b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64)
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(b)
```

Bytes `from..to` of `b`.

Example:

```bastio
let line = bfrom("key=value");
print_span(con, line, 4, 9);   // value
print_nl(con);
print_bytes(con, line);
print_nl(con);
let mut t = text_new();
text_push_str(&mut t, "a text");
print_text(con, t);
print_nl(con);
vec_free(t);
bfree(line);
```
